review_notes: I read the whole file and the statement of Matrix.exists_eq_mul_diagonal_mul_of_forall_mem_adicCompletionIntegers. I also checked the other candidate duplications. The valuation-log extraction appears in exists_zpow_mul_valued_eq_one and exists_valued_eq_exp, the nonzero-valuation pattern in q_ne_zero' and natCast_ne_zero_of_ne, and the symmetric Or.inl/Or.inr branches in `main`. All of these are short or are branch duplication, so I did not report them. The one reportable duplication is the 'apply the Smith-form matrix lemma and repackage the result as units in K0' step. The file's imports already cover everything the shared lemma needs. I did not compile the proposed lemma, so its exact proof is a sketch.

  have hk₂ : k₂ ∈ K0 𝔳 := ⟨hK₂, hK₂i⟩
  have hg'eq : g' = k₁ * diagSnd (piK r hr) * k₂ := by

findings.problem: Both theorems run the same argument. They call Matrix.exists_eq_mul_diagonal_mul_of_forall_mem_adicCompletionIntegers at 𝔳 with q_mem_asIdeal. They destructure its 13-component output. They rebuild the two matrices as units ⟨K, Ki, e, e'⟩. They prove membership in K0 𝔳 from the two integrality facts. They prove the unit equation by Units.ext, Units.val_mul and coe_diagSnd_piK. The code is the same in exists_mem_K0_eq_latticeMap_mul_diagSnd (lines 545–558, with g') and in exists_ψ_nv_eq (lines 704–709, with ψ nv). The only difference is the matrix being decomposed. The dependent hypotheses (h1, h2, hY, hpYi, hYi, hpY) are fed to the matrix lemma in the same shape both times. This is the 'unit Smith decomposition at the prime' step, written out twice.
findings.proposed_change:
Add one lemma in the Neighbours section, after coe_diagSnd_piK and K0 and before exists_mem_K0_eq_latticeMap_mul_diagSnd:

theorem exists_mem_K0_mul_diagSnd_mul (Y : (M₂)ˣ)
    (hY : ∀ i j, (Y : M₂) i j ∈ 𝓞v)
    (hpYi : ∀ i j, (((r:ℕ):𝕂) • ((Y⁻¹ : (M₂)ˣ) : M₂)) i j ∈ 𝓞v)
    (hYi : ¬ ∀ i j, ((Y⁻¹ : (M₂)ˣ) : M₂) i j ∈ 𝓞v)
    (hpY : ¬ ∀ i j, (((r:ℕ):𝕂)⁻¹ • (Y : M₂)) i j ∈ 𝓞v) :
    ∃ k₁ ∈ K0 𝔳, ∃ k₂ ∈ K0 𝔳, Y = k₁ * diagSnd (piK r hr) * k₂

Proof sketch: this is the current lines 545–558 and 704–709, moved into the lemma and applied to Y and Y⁻¹. Obtain K₁, K₁i, K₂, K₂i from Matrix.exists_eq_mul_diagonal_mul_of_forall_mem_adicCompletionIntegers r hr 𝔳 (q_mem_asIdeal r hr) (Y:M₂) ((Y⁻¹:(M₂)ˣ):M₂) with h1 := by rw [← Units.val_mul, mul_inv_cancel, Units.val_one] and h2 the analogue. Package k₁ := ⟨K₁,K₁i,e₁,e₁'⟩ and k₂ likewise. Take membership in K0 as ⟨hK₁,hK₁i⟩ and ⟨hK₂,hK₂i⟩. Close the equation with Units.ext, Units.val_mul, coe_diagSnd_piK, hYeq.

Use in exists_mem_K0_eq_latticeMap_mul_diagSnd: the block from `obtain ⟨K₁, …⟩` to `have hg'eq` becomes `obtain ⟨k₁, hk₁, k₂, hk₂, hg'eq⟩ := exists_mem_K0_mul_diagSnd_mul r hr g' hY hpYi hYi hpY`. The h1/h2 haves (needed only by the matrix lemma) can then be deleted. The rest is unchanged: `refine ⟨k₁, hk₁, ?_⟩; rw [← hc, hg'eq, …]`.

Use in exists_ψ_nv_eq: apply the lemma to Y := ψ nv. Coe of ψ nv is φ (ev 𝔳 n) by coe_ψ and coe_units_map_ev, both rfl. For the inverse, coe_units_map_ev_inv gives ev 𝔳 (n⁻¹) after map_inv. Feed hloc.1, hloc.2.1, hloc.2.2.1, hloc.2.2.2 after rewriting with these coercions, with `change` if needed. The local e1/e2 become redundant. The existential `⟨k₁, hk₁, k₂, hk₂, _⟩` is then exactly the lemma's conclusion, so the theorem becomes about 6 lines.
findings.benefit: The only nontrivial algebra step shared by the two neighbour arguments is stated once, so any change to the matrix lemma's interface needs one edit instead of two. The two callers then show their own mathematics: the lattice-sandwich hypotheses in one, the adelic/Hecke hypotheses in the other. Each loses about 10 lines of unit-wrapping boilerplate. The shared lemma also documents that every unit with the four integrality properties lies in K0 · diag(1,π) · K0.
